- When sentiment is negative or near-zero in recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model often lags; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops after spike), model tends to hold too high; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; increase forecast by 1–2% for last 5–7 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
